items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I joined Luis Russell again in 1931, replacing Otis Johnson.

ctx.x: I had started writing to my estranged wife and we decided to get together again, so she came from Cincinnati after I had been to Poughkeepsie about 3 weeks. The job went fine and Dewey was very happy because he had been able to bring a group to his home town. We got plenty of rest because there was not much activity in Poughkeepsie except for the park which had a dock on the Hudson river and excursion boats stopped there with tourists.

One day near the end of the season which was in September, I received a letter from my old buddy Higginbotham. He was playing with Luis Russell who was now at the Roseland Ballroom where Fletcher had worked and Higgy told me that he could get me in Russell's orchestra. So when we finished in Poughkeepsie, I lost no time getting to New York. I took a room with a
woman that Mack Walker and I had stayed with before for my wife and myself. We could cook there and that was much better than having to eat in restaurants and cheaper for two people.
